question: Should you speak in tongues?
summary: 1 Corinthians 14:5 has Paul saying he wishes all the Corinthians spoke in tongues and that anyone who speaks in tongues edifies himself. A few verses later in 14:8-9 he ridicules unintelligible speech as a trumpet giving an uncertain sound — words spoken into the air. The same chapter both endorses and discourages the practice.

reconcile.connective: Commentators read the "wish" for tongues (14:5) as approval of real, intelligible speech — the trumpet-noise rebuke in 14:8-9 targets only unintelligible, uninterpreted use.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible reads this as a flat Yes/No: 14:2-5's endorsement of tongues against 14:8-9's trumpet-noise ridicule of unintelligible speech.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/tongues.html

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-1714), on 1 Corinthians 14:6
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry's note on 14:6 is the one commentary in the gathered set keyed to both cited ranges (14:2-5 and 14:8-9) at once, arguing throughout that Paul condemns only 'the ostentation of speaking unknown and unintelligible language,' not the gift of tongues he elsewhere wishes all had. Haley's An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874) does not treat this passage — confirmed by a full-text search of the archive.org OCR (examinationof00hale_djvu.txt) for 'tongue'/'tongues,' which returns no hits touching 1 Corinthians 14 at all.

excerpts.excerpt_text: "Now I wish you all to speak with tongues (so far am I from thus speaking through having any objection to tongues), but rather IN ORDER THAT (as my ulterior and higher wish for you) ye should prophesy." Tongues must therefore mean languages, not ecstatic, unintelligible rhapsodie (as NEANDER fancied): for Paul could never "wish" for the latter in their behalf.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly ties 14:5's 'wish' to real, intelligible languages, not the unintelligible noise 14:8-9 mocks, so the wish and the rebuke are not aimed at the same thing.
